# Sample reasons for judgment (invented, for testing only)

The chambers judge began by setting out the procedural history of the dispute and the narrow question the parties had agreed to place before the court.

A party who seeks to rely on a limitation defence must raise it in a pleading, and must do so with enough particulars that the opposing party can meet it. The court will not infer the defence from silence. Where the pleading is deficient, the ordinary remedy is an amendment on terms - not the striking of the claim, and not a "deemed admission" of the underlying facts.

Applying that principle to the record before him, the judge concluded that the defence had been pleaded adequately and dismissed the application with costs in the cause.
